verdict.rationale: Kick documents an MCP/CLI surface where an AI agent can query transactions, categorize them, create rules, and execute bookkeeping changes with user approval, and the docs explicitly mention automating month-end checks. Kick also has a native reconciliation workflow, AI transfer matching logged under a Kick agent, low-confidence transactions left for manual review, and accountant-driven period locks. However, nothing documents an agent running the reconciliation itself end-to-end against bank statements and producing a close package for review. missing for 10: documented agent-driven reconciliation tools in MCP, explicit exception-flagging output for reconciliation discrepancies, an agent-prepared close/review package, and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can have an agent reconcile a month end-to-end, matching transactions, flagging exceptions, and preparing the close for human review

citations.quote: Connect MCP or CLI to take it further: query your client data in plain language, automate month-end checks, and build workflows that run across every workspace.
Your AI can query transactions, generate reports, and update bookkeeping — all with your approval.
automated categorization, transfer matching, and other AI actions are logged under the relevant Kick agent
When Kick's confidence is low, the transaction is left uncategorized for you to review manually
Reconciliation verifies that the transactions Kick has on record for an account actually match what the bank has on record - same amounts, same dates, no missing transactions, no duplicates.
When your accountant finishes reviewing and closing a period, they lock it.
